physical_interpretation: In low-spin wobbling landmark nucleus 135Pr, Matta et al. 2015 claimed discovery of transverse wobbling based on large E2/M1 mixing ratios (|delta| > 1) giving E2 dominance (60.6% and 70.3% for 747 and 813 keV) and a massive B(E2)out/B(E2)in ratio of 0.843(32) for the 813-keV line. However, Lv et al. 2022 performed high-statistics linear polarization (P) and angular correlation (Rac) measurements in JUROGAM II, conclusively proving that the true solutions are |delta| < 1 (-0.47 and -0.37), which collapses the E2 fraction down to only 18.1% and 12.0%, and reduces the extracted B(E2)out/B(E2)in for 813 keV from 0.843 down to 0.12(8) — a CATASTROPHIC FACTOR-OF-7.0 COLLAPSE! Similarly, the 450-keV line connecting the putative two-phonon band drops to just 8.8% E2. This collapse of E2 strength below single-particle levels completely ruled out the transverse wobbling interpretation of 135Pr, resolving it into tilted precession / single-particle alignment competition. This provides the ultimate Day 18 cautionary benchmark: transition strength extraction and collective band classification are entirely hostage to multipole-mixing determination; a false assignment of delta roots can fabricate phantom collective excitations.
